overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation on the voucher-reading and outside-meeting signing allegations, and declined to review the delegation and conflict-of-interest allegations as outside the law's scope.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the commission improperly delegated authority to one member to approve and sign payroll and accounts payable vouchers.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not govern whether a public body can delegate its authority to single member of the Commission; therefore we decline to review the allegation that the Commission improperly delegated its authority to approve and sign the Commission's payroll and accounts payable vouchers.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the commission fails to openly read and approve vouchers at its meetings.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, it is within the Commission's discretion whether to read and approve vouchers during its meetings, and its failure to do so did not violate the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged one member signs the commission's vouchers outside of meetings, which is improper.
allegations.key_passage: Furthermore, while the alleged act took place outside of an open meeting, because it did not involve communication between or among a quorum of the Commission, there was no deliberation and no violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged a commission member has a conflict of interest by serving on the Board of Selectmen and other town public bodies.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law does not govern conflicts of interests.

note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
